content:
The test image shows:
- Young soybean seedlings/plants that have completely collapsed and died
- Brown, papery, desiccated leaves curled and still attached to stems
- Dark discoloration at the stem base/soil line
- Multiple plants affected in a localized area
- Nearby plants still green (healthy)

This pattern — early seedling death, complete plant collapse with brown curled leaves remaining attached, dark stem near soil — is most consistent with **Pythium damping-off** (pre/post-emergence damping off with collapsed, dead seedlings). The Rhizoctonia reference shows more hypocotyl lesion-focused symptoms (reddish-brown canker on stem), whereas this shows complete plant death typical of Pythium.
